trailheadDirection: From Buckley, drive SR-165 south through Carbonado; just past the Carbon River Gorge bridge, bear right onto Mowich Lake Road and follow it about 17 miles, the last 13 or so on gravel, to the lake and trailhead. The road is gated at the park boundary in winter.
unverifiedNote: Sources disagree on which side of the lake the trailhead sits and on the gravel length.

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive east on Paradise Road about 14 miles; the signed Narada Falls parking lot is on the right, about 1 mile before the Paradise area.
unverifiedNote: Mileage varies slightly between sources (14 to 14.7); winter chain and nightly closure rules apply on this road.

trailhead: NF-38 (Forest Service Road 38) / Middle Fork Nooksack
trailheadDirection: From SR-542 about 3 miles east of Deming, turn right onto Mosquito Lake Road, go 4.8 miles, then turn left onto Middle Fork Road (FR-38) and follow it about 12.3 miles to where the road begins switchbacking uphill; park there, or sooner if snow stops you.
unverifiedNote: An older source reported a winter gate at Wallace Creek; not confirmed current. Exact parking spot for the Lincoln climb is not confirmed.

trailhead: No separate trailhead — over Mount Crowder by its Southwest Route
unverifiedNote: Not a trailhead; this entry names a route, and no drive route could be sourced for it.

trailheadDirection: From Entiat, drive Entiat River Road up the valley about 32 miles, turning right onto FR-5606 two miles past Silver Falls campground; follow FR-5606 steeply uphill about 4 miles to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: The trail was listed closed for the Little Giant Fire (WTA note dated 2026-07-30); the road's status was not stated. Early-season snow can block the upper road.

trailhead: North Fork Quinault Trailhead (North Shore Road)
trailheadDirection: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.
unverifiedNote: A WTA news item dated 2026-10-22 says the North Shore Road temporary bridge near Lake Quinault is out for the winter; whether that blocks this trailhead is unconfirmed.

trailhead: North Fork Quinault Trailhead / Ranger Station
trailheadDirection: From US-101 at milepost 126, turn onto South Shore Road and follow it 12.9 miles to the Quinault River bridge; cross it, turn right onto North Shore Road, and drive 3.5 miles to the road end at the trailhead and ranger station.
unverifiedNote: A WTA news item dated 2026-10-22 says the North Shore Road temporary bridge near Lake Quinault is out for the winter; whether that blocks this trailhead is unconfirmed.

trailheadDirection: From Darrington, drive south on the Mountain Loop Highway (FR-20) to Sloan Creek Road (FR-49) on the left, then follow FR-49 about 6.6 miles to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: Trail was listed closed for the Red Mountain Fire (WTA note dated 2025-09-03); road status itself not confirmed.

trailheadDirection: From Port Angeles, take Race Street south onto Hurricane Ridge Road and climb to the Hurricane Ridge parking area; turn sharply left onto the gravel Obstruction Point Road and follow it about 8 miles to its end at the trailhead. The gravel road is generally open only from mid-July to October.
unverifiedNote: Road can close without notice for weather or damage; current status not checked.

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive east on Paradise Road through Longmire about 19 miles to the Paradise parking area. From November 1 through winter the road above Longmire closes nightly.

From SR-20 just past milepost 82, turn north onto Baker Lake Road and follow it about 12 miles, turn left onto FR-12, and after about 3.5 miles turn right onto FR-13, which runs to the trailhead parking at its end.
unverifiedNote: Sources give different mileages for the FR-13 leg (about 3.5 to 5.5).

trailhead: PCT Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (Exit 52, Alpental Rd)
trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 52; the trailhead is at the end of the gravel ski-area parking lot, reached by turning left under the freeway and taking the first right from the eastbound off-ramp, or by turning right and immediately right again from the westbound off-ramp.

From Cle Elum, drive SR-903 north past Cle Elum Lake and turn left onto FR-46 (Cooper Lake Road) just before Salmon la Sac; follow FR-46 about 4.7 miles, turn right onto FR-4616, and continue about 1 mile to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: The distance from the Cooper Lake junction to the final turn differs between sources.

trailhead: Pinnacle Peak Trailhead (Reflection Lakes, Stevens Canyon Road)
trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive Paradise Road about 15 miles to the Stevens Canyon Road junction, turn right and go 1.5 miles to the Reflection Lakes parking area; the trailhead is on the south side of the road.
unverifiedNote: Stevens Canyon Road is closed in winter; opening dates not checked. The lot holds roughly 35 cars.

trailheadDirection: From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east about 14 miles; the trailhead parking is on the right between mileposts 134 and 135.
unverifiedNote: SR-20 closes east of this point for winter; this lot is just past the western gate.

trailheadDirection: From Mazama, take Lost River Road, which becomes FR-5400 where the pavement ends, and follow the gravel road to Harts Pass; the Slate Pass trailhead is at the second switchback on the road beyond Harts Pass.
unverifiedNote: WTA lists the Slate Peak hike closed for the Ptarmigan Fire (note dated 2026-07-31); road status unconfirmed. Trailers are barred June to December.

trailhead: Sol Duc Trailhead (end of Sol Duc Hot Springs Road)
trailheadDirection: From US-101 about 28 miles west of Port Angeles, turn onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road and follow it about 13.8 miles, past the park entrance station and the resort, to the road end and trailhead parking.
unverifiedNote: The road closes seasonally in winter; current 2026-27 status not confirmed. The 28-mile turnoff distance is from Port Angeles per one source.

trailheadDirection: From US-101 about 28 miles west of Port Angeles, turn onto Sol Duc Hot Springs Road and follow it about 13.8 miles, past the park entrance station and the resort, to the road end and trailhead parking.

No source names this pullout with a milepost; only a wide pullout near the State Creek crossing west of Washington Pass was found, with no road detail.

trailhead: SR 20 pullout (1.5 mi W of pass)
unverifiedNote: No source confirmed a pullout 1.5 miles west of the pass for the Cutthroat South Buttress; the only nearby 1.5 mile figure belongs to a different trailhead.

trailheadDirection: From Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east past the hairpin turn to the next major pullout, near milepost 166; park there.
unverifiedNote: Sources disagree on which side of the highway the pullout is on, so no side is stated.

trailhead: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout / Burgundy Col climbers' trail
trailheadDirection: From Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east past the hairpin turn to the next major pullout, near milepost 166; park there.
unverifiedNote: Sources disagree on which side of the highway the pullout is on, so no side is stated.

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.

From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 10 miles to an unsigned right turn near milepost 58.7, just past the old railroad community of Scenic; cross the railroad tracks, turn right, and follow the narrow dirt road about 0.3 mile to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: Trains can block the crossing.

trailheadDirection: From Skykomish, drive US-2 east about 12 miles; just as the highway crests a deep curve over Tunnel Creek, turn right onto FR-6095 (possible only from the eastbound lane) and go about 1.3 miles to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: Another source gives 1.5 miles on FR-6095; the road is rough with potholes.

trailheadDirection: From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park, turn onto Louella Road, then Palo Alto Road, which becomes FR-28 at the forest boundary; turn right onto FR-2880, stay left onto FR-2870, and continue to the trailhead parking just past the Dungeness River bridge.
unverifiedNote: WTA (updated 2025-12-29) reports a rockslide on FR-2880 near Dungeness Forks Campground while saying the trails remain reachable via FR-2870; current road state unconfirmed.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw, drive SR-410 east to the White River entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, turn right onto Sunrise Road and go about 5 miles, cross the White River, then turn left onto White River Road and follow it to its end at the campground. White River Road closes for the winter.
unverifiedNote: Mileage on SR-410 and Sunrise Road differs slightly between sources, so those are not stated.
